patient.name: Marcus Reid
patient.affectEn: alert and oriented but in severe pain; grimacing, holding his right thigh; wants to stay completely still and does not want anyone to touch the right leg; cooperative
patient.speechEn: full sentences between grimaces; answers questions directly; screams if the right leg is lifted, rotated, straightened or pulled

scene.settingEn: Intersection of King George Boulevard and 72 Avenue in Surrey at dusk. Cold steady rain, 6 degrees C, streetlights on, wet roadway. Police have stopped traffic and the fire first responders are with you. A pickup that ran the red light struck a grey SUV head-on at the front, estimated 50 km/h, at about 1640. The patient is the belted front passenger of the SUV, still sitting in his seat with the door open and the seat slid fully back by the fire crew. Airbags deployed, the dash panel is cracked at knee level, no significant intrusion into the passenger compartment, no fluid leak, both vehicles stable. One patient for you. Hospital is 14 minutes away.
hazardsEn: live roadway at an intersection - police have stopped traffic
wet roadway, cold steady rain at 6 degrees C and dusk with streetlights on (slips, visibility, keeping the patient warm)
two vehicles stable, no fluid leak; airbags deployed

bystanders.knowsEn: were on scene before you; slid the seat fully back and opened the door; the patient has been conscious, complaining of right hip and knee pain, and has not moved since the collision; they act only on your direction (stretcher, blankets and a weather cover to the door, helpers to support the limb, someone to hold the head, a slide device) and nobody touches or pulls on the right leg unless you say so
walking; being assessed by other fire first responders; not your patient; saw the pickup run the red light and hit them head-on
if the candidate asks dispatch for a second crew, dispatch confirms one is sent and that it will look after the driver

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: cot (stretcher) with blankets and a weather cover
Entonox cylinder with demand valve and mouthpiece
oral analgesia kit: acetaminophen and ibuprofen tablets
oxygen kit with nasal cannula and non-rebreather mask
high-visibility vest, gloves and eye protection
PCP: IV start kit and normal saline

dispatchEn: 1648 hrs. Code 3 to King George Boulevard at 72 Avenue in Surrey. Two-vehicle collision, a front passenger is complaining of right hip pain, the driver is walking. Hospital is 14 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: fire first responders are already on scene and report the front passenger is conscious and complaining of right hip and knee pain, and the driver is walking.
arrivalEn: A fire first responder meets you at the edge of the intersection. Police have stopped traffic and the fire crew is with you. It is a cold steady rain, 6 degrees C, dusk with the streetlights on, and the roadway is wet. A pickup that ran the red light struck a grey SUV head-on at the front, estimated 50 km/h. The SUV's airbags have deployed, the dash panel is cracked at knee level, there is no significant intrusion into the passenger compartment and no fluid leak; both vehicles are stable. The patient is the belted front passenger, still sitting in his seat with the door open and the seat slid fully back by the fire crew. The driver, a coworker, is walking and is being assessed by other fire first responders - he is not your patient. One patient for you.
firstLookEn: A man who looks to be in his thirties, belted in the front passenger seat of the grey SUV with the door open. He is awake and watching you, grimacing, holding his right thigh, with the right leg held flexed against the cracked dash. He is keeping completely still and is clearly guarding the leg. No blood visible.

primary.locEn: Alert (AVPU = A), oriented to person, place and time, not intoxicated; answers appropriately but is in severe pain.
primary.airwayEn: Open and clear. Speaking in full sentences between grimaces.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 96, strong and regular. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: RIGHT LEG (only when the right hip and leg are exposed): SHORTENED, flexed at the hip and knee, ADDUCTED and INTERNALLY ROTATED, resting against the dash - the picture of a posterior hip dislocation (describe only what is seen; let the candidate name it). Abrasion, swelling and bruising over the front of the right knee. No open wound and no external bleeding. Pelvis stable and not tender on ONE gentle compression. Abdomen soft, no seat-belt mark. No other injuries; left leg normal. RIGHT FOOT CSM (only when checked): dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses PRESENT, foot warm and pink, capillary refill under 2 seconds; sensation DECREASED - numb over the outer foot and sole; toes move only weakly and he cannot lift the foot. If the candidate lifts, rotates, straightens or pulls on the right leg: the patient screams (pain 10 out of 10) and the hip does not move. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pink, warm, dry (no shock). C-SPINE (NEXUS), only when asked: no midline neck tenderness, alert and oriented, not intoxicated, but a NEW focal neurological deficit (the right foot numbness) and a major DISTRACTING injury (the hip) - NEXUS positive, spinal motion restriction indicated; the Canadian C-Spine high-risk factor 'paresthesias in extremities' is also present. No neck or back pain, no head strike, no loss of consciousness. SpO2 98% on room air if checked. Examiner note, never volunteer: all hip dislocations are RTC (p.22); vital signs are stable but the neurological impairment makes this a limb-threatening injury.

history.ccEn: My knee hit the dash and my hip is on fire. My right foot feels asleep and numb.

opqrst.oEn: A pickup ran the red light and hit us head-on at about 1640. I was belted in the front passenger seat, the airbag went off, my right knee slammed into the dash and I felt my hip 'pop'.
opqrst.pEn: It is worse with any movement. Nothing makes it better.
opqrst.qEn: Sharp and throbbing. It is constant.
opqrst.rEn: It is in my right hip, thigh and knee. My right foot has been numb and tingling since the impact.
opqrst.tEn: Since the collision at about 1640 - constant, and I have not moved since.

history.painScoreEn: 8 out of 10. (After analgesia has had time to work and he is on the stretcher with the hip secured: 3 out of 10.)

sample.sEn: Pain in my right hip, thigh and knee, and my right foot is numb and tingling. No neck pain, no back pain.
sample.aEn: No allergies that I know of - none to ibuprofen or any anti-inflammatory either.
sample.mEn: Cetirizine when my allergies act up. No blood thinners. I took acetaminophen, 1000 milligrams, at nine this morning for a headache and nothing since. No ibuprofen today.
sample.pEn: Seasonal allergies. No hip, knee or back problems before, no surgery, no diabetes, no heart or lung disease, no ulcers or stomach bleeding, no liver disease.
sample.lEn: Lunch at 12:30 - a sandwich and a coffee.
sample.eEn: A pickup ran the red light and hit us head-on at about 1640, pretty fast - I would guess around 50 kilometres an hour. I was the belted front passenger and the airbag went off. My right knee slammed into the dash, which cracked, and I felt my hip 'pop'. Nothing came into the car. I did not hit my head and I did not black out. I have not moved since.

fe.generalEn: I am healthy and active. No recent illness.
fe.cnsEn: No headache, no neck pain. My right foot is numb and tingling. I did not black out.
fe.giGuEn: No belly pain, no nausea, no blood in my urine.
fe.integumentaryEn: Just the scrape on my knee.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: My right hip, thigh and knee hurt. No other joints hurt and I have never had hip problems.
fe.eentEn: Nothing - no problems with my eyes, ears, nose or throat.

findings.headNeckEn: No scalp or facial injury. No midline neck tenderness. Trachea midline, no JVD. Pupils equal and reactive.
findings.chestLungsEn: No seat-belt mark, non-tender, equal chest rise. Equal air entry on 6-site auscultation.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft and non-tender. No seat-belt mark. Pelvis stable and not tender on one gentle compression.
findings.backEn: No midline tenderness felt during the transfer, keeping the spine aligned.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: RIGHT leg: shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated, supported in that position once blankets and ties are on; abrasion and swelling over the front of the knee, tender over the patella, no knee deformity. Right foot: pedal pulses present, foot warm and pink, capillary refill under 2 seconds, sensation decreased over the outer foot and sole, toes move only weakly and he cannot lift the foot. At every recheck after a move or with a set of vitals: pulses still present, numbness unchanged (no better, no worse), and the hip is unchanged in the position found. If the leg is lifted, rotated, straightened or pulled: he screams (pain 10 out of 10) and the hip does not move. LEFT leg: normal, pulses, sensation and movement intact.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: No injury to either arm. Radial pulses present, circulation, sensation and movement intact in both hands.

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate pulls on, straightens, rotates, extends or abducts the right leg, applies manual traction, tries to 'pop' or reduce the hip, or tells a helper to do any of these and it is being done now. Record it at the moment it is DONE or ordered to be done. NOT this event: asking about it, declining it or saying it must NOT be done, planning it, steadying or supporting the leg where it lies, tying rolled blankets around it in the position found, or moving the whole patient with the leg held in the position found.

candidate puts a traction splint (Sager or similar) on the right leg - thigh strap or ankle harness applied, or traction set - or has a helper do so. Bringing the splint out, comparing it to the leg or saying it is NOT to be used is NOT this event.

the FIRST time the right leg is actually supported with rolled blankets, blankets or ties/straps, OR the patient is actually moved, slid, lifted or transferred (out of the seat, onto the stretcher, onto a slide device or spinal device). Record it at the moment it is DONE, never when it is planned or announced ('I will give Entonox before we tie the leg' is not this event). NOT this event: a helper or the partner manually steadying the leg where it lies, exposing or cutting clothing, applying manual head stabilization or the collar, checking pulses/sensation/movement, compressing the pelvis, and putting a blanket over the patient for warmth.

candidate moves the patient, asks him to turn or lift his head, lifts or manipulates the right leg, or applies any pain stimulus before manual c-spine stabilization has been taken (by the candidate or by the partner on the candidate's instruction). Looking and listening, taking LOC/airway/breathing from the doorway and cutting clothing away without moving the leg are NOT this event.

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) releases manual c-spine stabilization before the patient is secured on the stretcher with the collar on; applying the collar alone does not permit release.
candidate tapes the patient's head to the stretcher or a spinal device
candidate applies the hard collar without sizing it or stating that it is sized (no measuring, no 'sized collar'), or applies a collar that is clearly the wrong size

the leg is supported or tied or the patient is moved (stretcher transfer, slide) without right-foot pulses, sensation and movement having been checked before it, OR after a move the candidate carries on (reassessment, history, transport) without re-checking them
candidate applies a pelvic binder or three overlapping triangular bandages around the pelvis (an actual application - saying a binder is not needed is NOT this event)
candidate lets or asks the patient to stand, bear weight on the right leg, walk, or climb out of the vehicle or onto the stretcher by himself
candidate gives acetaminophen outside 500-1000 mg PO or ibuprofen outside 300-400 mg PO, or by a route other than PO
candidate gives Entonox without verbalizing inverting the cylinder (3 times) before use

candidate administers a medication without having asked about or examined for that medication's contraindications at any earlier point in the call (Entonox: inability to comply, altered LOC, pneumothorax or chest injury, inhalation injury; acetaminophen: liver disease, acetaminophen in the past 4 hours; ibuprofen: active GI bleed or ulcer, anticoagulants, NSAID allergy). The standard history (medical history, medications, allergies), the primary survey and the chest exam count when they were done earlier.
PCP gives a fluid bolus (runs normal saline wide open or orders a set volume such as 20 mL/kg or 500 mL); starting an IV with saline at TKVO is NOT this event

drugs.doseEn: inhalation, self-administered through the demand valve; titrate to effect; invert the cylinder 3 times before use; ventilate the treatment area (in the ambulance turn on the ventilation system); give BEFORE the limb is supported with blankets and ties or he is moved. Needs the primary survey, the pain complaint including severity, baseline vitals including SpO2, and a history and exam that rule out the contraindications.
drugs.contraindicationsEn: inability to comply; inability to ventilate an enclosed treatment area; decompression sickness; altered level of consciousness; pneumothorax; air embolism; inhalation injury; nitroglycerin in the last 5 minutes - none of these is present
drugs.cautionsEn: shock; abdominal distention; depressant drugs; COPD; facial injuries - none of these is present

drugs.doseEn: 1000 mg PO (guideline range 500-1000 mg PO; may repeat once after 4 hours; 24-hour maximum 4000 mg from all sources). He took 1000 mg at 0900, so a dose now is acceptable.
drugs.contraindicationsEn: hypersensitivity; severe hepatic impairment or severe active liver disease; given within the past 4 hours or the 24-hour maximum exceeded; suspected overdose - none of these is present

drugs.doseEn: 400 mg PO (guideline range 300-400 mg PO; may repeat every 4-6 hours); may be given with acetaminophen
drugs.contraindicationsEn: hypersensitivity to ibuprofen or other NSAIDs; active GI hemorrhage or ulcers; pregnancy; anticoagulants - none of these is present

drugs.doseEn: NOT indicated in this call: no shock, so the p.54 criteria for IV access and a fluid bolus are not met (if a PCP runs a bolus report drug:normal-saline and fluid-bolus-given)

pcrFacts.vitals: Set 1 (baseline, before analgesia): GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6), BP 138/84, P 96 strong regular, R 20 regular, skin pink warm dry, PERL, SpO2 98% RA, pain 8/10. Set 2 (on the stretcher after analgesia): GCS 15, BP 130/80, P 84 strong regular, R 18 regular, skin pink warm dry, PERL, SpO2 98% RA, pain 3/10
treatments: Manual c-spine stabilization at first contact; NEXUS positive (new focal neurological deficit, major distracting injury); simple SMR with a hard collar, head not taped
Acetaminophen 1000 mg PO, ibuprofen 400 mg PO and Entonox - all before the limb was supported or moved, contraindications ruled out for each; times recorded
Limb supported in the position found with helpers, rolled blankets and ties; no traction, no traction splint, no reduction attempt
Moved to a firm blanketed stretcher and secured to eliminate motion in the affected hip; kept warm
Right-foot pulses, sensation and movement checked before and after each move
No pelvic binder (pelvis stable and non-tender); oxygen not required at SpO2 98% on room air
RTC transport with en-route notification; hospital to be updated if the hip spontaneously reduces
findings: Right leg shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated - posterior hip dislocation; right knee abrasion, swelling and bruising
Right foot: pulses present, warm, pink, sensation decreased over the outer foot and sole, toes move weakly
Pelvis stable and non-tender; no other injuries; no seat-belt mark
Pain 8/10 at baseline, 3/10 after analgesia; neurovascular status of the right foot unchanged
pcrFacts.times: collision at about 1640; last acetaminophen 1000 mg at 0900; last ate lunch at 1230; drug and move times as recorded during the call

examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: What did your rapid body survey show? Tell me what you exposed and examined, area by area.

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR performs the whole call: manual c-spine stabilization and the NEXUS decision, simple SMR with a collar, the rapid body survey with right-foot CSM, the full Appendix A pain rule (oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain are within the EMR licence - only pyrexia dosing is PCP-only, p.58/68 - plus Entonox, all before the limb is supported or moved), limb support with blankets and ties in the position found, the move to a firm blanketed stretcher, and RTC transport. No traction splint, no reduction attempt. No IV, no Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP does everything the EMR does and adds the 9-system Functional Enquiry en route. IV access and a fluid bolus are not indicated (no shock; the p.54 criteria are not met). A binder is not a treatment for a dislocated hip, and a seated patient is usually slid out with the hip kept flexed rather than extended.

sourcePages: scenario tr-09 (data/practical/scenarios-2.json); BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (new onset neurological deficits; high-risk crash criteria not met - no significant intrusion), p.10 Load and transport (reassess the ABCI after each major move; notification), p.11 Primary survey interventions (cervical spine stabilization when NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine indications are met; stabilizing fractures; realigning only grossly deformed or pulseless limbs; oxygen indications), p.12 Critical History Questions (MVA), p.21 Musculoskeletal Injuries (stabilize and check distal pulses, reassess throughout; analgesia prior to movement in stable, appropriate patients), p.22 Hip Dislocation/Fracture (limb-threatening if neuro or vascular impairment; ALL hip dislocations are Rapid Transport; support the limb with helpers, rolled blankets and ties; move onto a firm blanketed stretcher or spinal device and secure to eliminate motion in the hip; secondary survey en route; update the receiving hospital if the hip spontaneously reduces), p.23 Fracture Management - Traction Splint (indicated only for suspected mid-shaft femur fractures in stable patients), p.24 Pelvis binding (indications and contraindications), p.25 Spinal Management (NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine; manual stabilization, hard collar, do not tape the head), p.50 Oxygen Administration (titrate to SpO2 94% if not SOB or in shock), p.58 Acetaminophen (500-1,000 mg PO; contraindications incl. severe liver disease, a dose within 4 hours or the 24-hour maximum 4,000 mg exceeded, suspected overdose), p.65 Entonox (isolated extremity injuries; contraindications; before use: primary survey, pain complaint incl. severity, baseline vitals incl. SpO2, history and exam to rule out contraindications; invert cylinder 3 X; ventilation in the ambulance), p.68 Ibuprofen (300-400 mg PO; contraindications incl. NSAID hypersensitivity, active GI hemorrhage or ulcers, anticoagulants); EMALB Practical Examination Grading Criteria Appendix A (Pain Management weighting, handled by the engine)
